Sarah (Sales): Hey team — Acme's POC goes live Tue. They want temporary extra headroom on their dedicated pool (dp-58) for a 36h demo spike. Need: +2 GPUs burst starting 2024-05-20 09:00 UTC, ephemeral API keys for their SREs, and a quick cost estimate. Can ops provision and confirm access details?
Alex (Solutions): Quick Qs: expected concurrent requests / QPS, which model & quantization, and target latency SLO?
Maya (Acme): Expect ~160 concurrent requests during the demo window. Using open-llama-30b (4-bit quant), typical seq length ~1024, aiming for p50 < 300ms.
Priya (EngInfra): We can do that. Suggest setting burst_up_to = 2 GPUs (so pool can hit 6 GPUs total) for 48h window to be safe. Policy we normally apply: cooldown 30m, autoscale-window 5m, and a hard cap to prevent accidental over-provisioning.
Priya (EngInfra): Console path: Console -> Dedicated -> Pools -> dp-58 -> Edit -> Temporary Burst. Or via API:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/dedicated/pools/dp-58/burst
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $RDW_TOKEN"
 -H "Content-Type: application/json"
 -d '{"burst_max_gpus":2,"duration_hours":48,"start_time":"2024-05-20T09:00:00Z","cooldown_minutes":30}'```
Sarah (Sales): Nice. Priya, can you confirm whether that will affect other customers on the same host cluster? Need to be sure it's isolated for the POC.
Priya (EngInfra): The dedicated pool is isolated to the account. Burst uses reserved slack / headroom in the same pool; it won't evict other customers. If we need extra isolation we can pin instances to a burst-only allocation, but that's not required here.
Sarah (Sales): Thanks. Finance — any rough numbers to quote Acme before the demo?
Finance Bot: Quick estimate: 2 extra GPUs * 48 hours = 96 GPU-hours. At $4.50 / GPU-hour => ~$432. We can apply a $500 POC credit to cover this, so the customer cost would be $0 for the burst period if approved. (Finalize on the invoice).
Alex (Solutions): Also recommend setting a fallback model policy in case we hit limits: route to open-llama-13b-quant for non-critical requests. That reduces cost/latency and keeps the demo stable.
Priya (EngInfra): Regarding SRE access: we'll create an ephemeral service account and scoped API key that expires after 72h. Command (RDW CLI):```rdw iam create-key --service-account poc-acme-sre --scopes "dedicated:pool:dp-58" --expires-in 72h``` Key will only have pool-level actions (submit, tail logs, metrics).
Sarah (Sales): Perfect. Can we also ip-allowlist their CI runners? They asked to limit keys to their office IPs.
Priya (EngInfra): Yes — when creating the key we can attach allowlist: e.g., --allowed-ips 198.51.100.0/24. We'll include that.
Deploy Bot: Provisioning job started: job-id jb-20240514-77. Applying burst policy to dp-58.
Deploy Bot: Burst policy applied ✅. Created ephemeral key id poc-acme-sre-01 (expires 2024-05-23T09:00:00Z). Logs: https://console.redwood.ai/pools/dp-58/events/jb-20240514-77
Maya (Acme): Verified access from our SREs, ran perf smoke tests — p50 ~220ms, no errors. Thanks for the fast turnaround :tada:
Sarah (Sales): Awesome. I'll mark the credit applied and send a short note to Acme with the access window + rotation reminder.
Priya (EngInfra): Reminder: burst will auto-stop at end_time. If they need an extension, open a ticket at least 6 hours before expiry and include justification + expected extra GPU-hours.
Alex (Solutions): I'll also add the fallback routing rule to their route config so demo traffic gracefully degrades.
Sarah (Sales): Closing loop — demo greenlit. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:
